video_title: Coin Streams: Cash-Flow Forecasting in Motion
learning_objectives: Complete a cash-flow forecast using net cash flow and closing balance rules
Explain why a profitable business can still run out of cash
Evaluate forecast limitations and short-term remedies

visual_beats.directive: Cafe crowd orders animate in
Till counter drops below the invoice
Invoice stamp flashes red
Coin stream label cash appears

scenes.voiceover_script: Lantern Lane City Cafes serves thousands of lunches, yet the owner cannot pay the milk supplier this Friday. Profit is revenue minus costs over a period; cash is money available now. A cash-flow forecast is an estimate of future cash inflows and outflows, usually month by month, showing the expected closing balance. A profitable business can still run out of cash when customers pay later and suppliers demand payment now. Follow the coin streams to find the gap.

elements.label: Cash inflows row with blue coins
Cash outflows row with orange coins

visual_beats.directive: Table rows draw themselves one by one
Blue coins enter the inflow row
Orange coins leave the outflow row
Balance row glows with the rule

scenes.voiceover_script: A cash-flow forecast has five features. Cash inflows are sums received, such as cafe takings. Cash outflows are sums paid, such as wages, rent and ingredients. Net cash flow is the difference between inflows and outflows during each period. Opening balance is cash at the start; closing balance is cash at the end. The rule is simple: closing balance equals opening balance plus net cash flow. Every row becomes a moving coin stream.

elements.label: Balance bar sixteen thousand then eleven thousand

visual_beats.directive: Opening balance eight thousand appears
Net flow plus eight thousand fills the bar
Month two outflow stream overtakes inflow
Bar settles at eleven thousand

scenes.voiceover_script: Build the forecast with Lantern Lane. Month one opens with eight thousand dollars. Inflows are thirty thousand; outflows are twenty-two thousand, so net cash flow is plus eight thousand and closing balance is sixteen thousand. Month two receives twenty-six thousand and pays thirty-one thousand, giving net cash flow of minus five thousand. Sixteen thousand plus negative five thousand leaves eleven thousand. Blue coins flow in, orange coins flow out, and the balance bar rises then dips.

elements.label: Month three and four inflow coins
Four net flows summed to minus twelve thousand

visual_beats.directive: Month three row highlights the ten thousand gap
Closing bar nearly reaches zero
Month four net flow turns the bar red
Axis shows negative four thousand

scenes.voiceover_script: Month three opens at eleven thousand. Inflows fall to twenty-four thousand, outflows climb to thirty-four thousand, so net cash flow is minus ten thousand and closing balance is one thousand. Month four opens at one thousand, receives twenty-eight thousand, pays thirty-three thousand, and ends four thousand dollars in the red. Add the four net flows: plus eight, minus five, minus ten, minus five equals minus twelve thousand. Eight thousand opening cash minus twelve thousand gives negative four thousand.

visual_beats.directive: Profit column builds from sales
Invoice tile floats but becomes no coin
Stock bags pile up in the middle
Cash column drains as bills land

scenes.voiceover_script: Why can a profitable cafe chain still have no cash? Because credit sales become trade receivables, not coins. Because extra coffee beans sit as inventory before they are sold. And because suppliers, wages and rent must be paid immediately. Profit measures performance over a period; cash measures survival this week. Therefore a growing business can report a healthy profit while its bank balance empties, so the forecast must track timing, not just totals.

visual_beats.directive: Cash coin enters the inventory node
Inventory moves into production
Receivable invoice turns into a coin
Working capital card shows five thousand

scenes.voiceover_script: The working capital cycle shows the same trap. Cash buys inventory; inventory moves into production and service delivery; sales create receivables; then customers finally pay and cash returns. Working capital is current assets minus current liabilities, the finance needed for day-to-day expenses. Lantern Lane holds twenty thousand dollars of current assets and fifteen thousand of current liabilities, so working capital is five thousand dollars. Too little working capital risks insolvency; too much sits idle.

visual_beats.directive: Negative four thousand bar appears
Overdraft tile lifts bar to plus one thousand
Supplier relationship tile wobbles
Customer goodwill tile dips slightly

scenes.voiceover_script: A negative closing balance signals a shortfall, so Lantern Lane needs a five-thousand-dollar overdraft. That facility covers the four-thousand-dollar gap and leaves one thousand dollars of headroom. Delaying supplier payments or asking customers to pay sooner also helps. An overdraft is flexible and quick, but interest charges grow if the gap lasts. Late payments strain supplier relationships and can stop deliveries. Asking customers to pay faster improves cash, yet may cost goodwill.

scenes.on_screen_title: What a Forecast Cannot Tell You

elements.label: Cold spell and broken oven surprises

visual_beats.directive: Estimate badges pop up on each cell
Surprise icons break two flow links
Warning light turns green before the gap
Split panel holds the judgement

scenes.voiceover_script: Forecasts have limits. They depend on estimates: a cold spell raises sales, a broken oven adds costs, and customers may pay late. A cash-flow forecast is not a profit forecast and cannot predict surprises. Used with care, it warns of a gap before it becomes a crisis, letting the owner obtain finance in time. Because timing decides survival, a small cafe with steady profit still watches every coin stream.

end_of_video_recap_quiz.question: Lantern Lane expects a closing balance of -$4,000 next month. Which response protects cash without damaging future trade most?
options: Buy a new delivery van now
Obtain a short-term overdraft and chase receivables
end_of_video_recap_quiz.visual_explanation: The balance bar dips below zero, then an overdraft tile lifts it above zero while invoice flows from customers turn into coins; the van and extra-stock tiles grey out.
